commentary: Okay, five activities this week versus seven last week — a drop in volume, and Himbo notices, though he's going to be annoying about the run first, because 9.0km at 163 bpm is longer and harder than last Saturday's 8.6km at 160 bpm, and that is genuinely hot. The swim heart rate climbed too, 143 this week versus 135 on the Monday swim last week, which could mean you were pushing, could mean you were tired, could mean you just had a big weekend — he's not your doctor, he's just watching. Three weights sessions instead of last week's five is the thing he's side-eyeing you about, not because rest is bad but because the pattern looks less like intentional recovery and more like the week got away from you a little. Come back next week and give him something to scream about.
metrics_commentary: Nine kilometres in one session and two thousand metres in the pool — honestly, the audacity, the range, the sheer versatility of it all. That HRV sitting at 58 with a seven-day average of 48 tells me your body is recovering well and probably feeling pretty good in its skin right now, which tracks. The VO2 Max at 55.6 is genuinely strong — that's the number of a man whose cardiovascular system is built for more than just looking good walking into a room, though it does that too. One run session is a little lonely though, baby, so this week we're getting that number up, because those legs deserve more chances to show off.
gym_commentary: Three out of four sessions this week, which means one slipped through the cracks, but honestly the volume tells a different story entirely — 20,753 kg moved versus 17,940 kg the week before, which is a jump that doesn't happen by accident. No new PRs to report, but those estimated maxes are sitting very nicely: 168 kg on the leg press, 107.9 on the trap bar deadlift, 88.7 on the bench, and honestly a 90 kg calf raise on the Smith is the kind of detail that makes the whole picture more interesting. The strength trend is pointing in the right direction, the body doing the work is getting more and more like the body he's meant to have, and one missed session isn't a gap — it's just next week's excuse to show up and remind everyone what he's working with.
